channel.title: ZeroTrace (EN)
channel.description: A daily cybersecurity newsletter: one concrete concept a day, for beginners and for those who want to go deeper.

item.title: The app you let into your Google account is still getting in, even if you stopped using it
item.description: Every "Sign in with Google" or "Allow access to your Gmail" leaves a key in the door. What each app can see, why changing your password doesn't always revoke it, and the five-minute review that does. — Critical: Xen Orchestra: an empty token grants admin access, already exploited | Heads-up: GeoServer: two flaws in a chain that leads to server takeover, already exploited | Heads-up: 1Password confirms customer data theft; your saved passwords aren't affected

item.title: No package gets released by paying through a text message link
item.description: Why your phone fills up with "package on hold" texts during the biggest shopping week of the year, what that $2 fee is really after, and the one rule that keeps you out of it. — Heads-up: Mitel MiCollab: five flaws in its conferencing component, one rated maximum severity, under attack | Heads-up: Juniper Session Smart Conductor: critical flaw grants root control, already exploited

item.title: The tablet the whole family uses shouldn't be signed in to your account
item.description: Why a shared iPad or Android tablet signed in to your personal account shows your messages and verification codes to whoever picks it up, how to separate it in ten minutes, and what you don't need to do. — Heads-up: NGINX: HTTP/2 flaw with public exploit code, now under attack per Singapore's CSA

item.title: The certificates that protect your PC's startup expired this year: make sure it has the new ones
item.description: What changed in Windows Secure Boot, why your computer still starts the same even if it isn't sorted yet, how to check in a minute, and what you don't need to touch. — Critical: Drupal: highly critical installer flaw lets attackers take over sites, already exploited | Heads-up: Firefox 161 fixes 110 flaws, 59 of them high impact

item.title: Your phone carries a number for tracking you across ads (and you can take it away)
item.description: Android and iPhone give each phone an advertising identifier that apps share. Deleting or denying it takes two minutes and cuts a big chunk of cross-app tracking, without breaking anything. — Heads-up: Chrome 158 gets an update that fixes a critical flaw

item.title: Who can turn on your laptop's camera and microphone
item.description: A sticker over the camera feels reassuring, but permissions are what actually decide who can see and hear you. How to review them in five minutes, and what to do if you get the "I recorded you" email.

item.title: Your router's admin page shouldn't be reachable from the internet
item.description: What "remote management" is, why attackers hunt for routers with that door open, how to check in five minutes that yours is closed, and why you don't need to touch anything else your internet provider manages. — Heads-up: WhatsApp fixes three flaws; one that exposed your IP address may have been used with spam messages | Heads-up: GnuPG: serious flaw in GPGME, the library behind Gpg4win and many encryption tools

item.title: Before you sell your smart speaker or robot vacuum, remove it from your account
item.description: Why the reset button isn't enough, what stays on the device and in the cloud (your Wi-Fi password, a map of your home, your history), and the two steps that wipe it clean in ten minutes, including when you're the one buying it used. — Critical: Apache Roller: critical flaw lets attackers take over the server without a password, already exploited | Critical: Cisco Expressway: hard-coded credentials give full control of clustered devices, already exploited | Heads-up: SAP NetWeaver Enterprise Portal: a flaw patched in November 2025, now under attack | Heads-up: PyPI: two fake versions of Microsoft's agent-framework stole developer credentials

item.title: Your WhatsApp chats only exist on your phone (and in the backup you make)
item.description: Why WhatsApp can't give your conversations back if you lose your phone, where your backup lives, who protects it, and how to encrypt it with your fingerprint in three minutes. — Heads-up: VMware vCenter: critical authentication bypass, attacked since September | Heads-up: PHP: update fixes 18 flaws, several critical, across every supported version

item.title: A smartwatch without a passcode shows your messages to whoever picks it up
item.description: What someone can see and do with your watch in hand, why Wrist Detection is the key piece, and the three settings that are enough. — Heads-up: Synology NAS: a 2024 flaw that hands over the device, now exploited

item.title: That third-party script on your website is your code, too
item.description: Analytics, A/B testing, chat widgets, ad pixels: every line you paste into your site runs with the same permissions as your own code. What happens when that vendor gets hit, and what's enough to keep it from taking you down with it. — Heads-up: Optimizely: websites of 178 organizations served code that stole cards and attacked out-of-date iPhones | Heads-up: Chrome 158 fixes 204 flaws, six of them critical

item.title: Even with the padlock, the network can see which sites you visit
item.description: What the internet's "phone book" gives away, who sees it at home or on public Wi-Fi, and how to encrypt it in two minutes for free.

item.title: Who can see where you are right now?
item.description: Sharing your location is handy, but it's easy to forget. How to check in five minutes who can see you on the map and cut off what no longer makes sense, without drama.

item.title: Your PC shouldn't run on the admin account every day
item.description: Why the account you browse, read email and game on should be a standard account, how to switch without locking yourself out, and what it won't fix.

item.title: A passkey for your email: the password nobody can phish
item.description: Why signing in to your main account with your phone's fingerprint or PIN stops phishing better than any code, and what to leave alone when you turn it on. — Heads-up: Check Point: Gaia OS flaw gives full control of the firewall, already exploited

item.title: Your TV gets security updates too (until one day it doesn't)
item.description: Why a smart TV needs patches just like your phone, how to let them install on their own, and what to do, without buying a new TV, when the manufacturer stops sending them.

item.title: Your home camera is only as secure as its app account
item.description: Why someone who wants to watch your cameras goes after your username and password, not the device, and the three app settings that stop them.

item.title: Having your files in the cloud isn't the same as having a backup
item.description: Why OneDrive, iCloud Drive, and Google Drive delete and encrypt right along with you, what safety net they really give you, and the copy you're missing. — Critical: Chrome: XML processing flaw already being exploited | Critical: Outlook: a crafted file hands over your password hash, already exploited

item.title: That bargain Android tablet may come with a stowaway installed at the factory
item.description: What an "uncertified" tablet is, why some arrive with a backdoor already on board, and the one-minute check to do before and after you buy.

item.title: That code to "vote" opens your WhatsApp to someone else
item.description: How the fake contest spreading on WhatsApp works, why the device-linking code is the key to your account, and one simple rule so you never fall for it. — Heads-up: OpenSSH on Alpine Linux: a very long password lets attackers log in without the real one

item.title: Your photos know where you took them
item.description: What data rides along hidden inside a photo, when it can give away where you live, and how to share pictures without handing out your home address. — Heads-up: Apple: a 2024 WebKit flaw now under attack on unpatched devices

item.title: If someone steals your phone after watching you type the passcode
item.description: Why your unlock passcode opens far more than the screen, what the theft protections on iPhone and Android actually do, and what to have ready before it happens. — Critical: SonicWall: SSL VPN flaw that bypasses SAML, now exploited | Heads-up: Zyxel GS1900 switches: exploited flaw that slipped past the earlier patch

item.title: Your Windows 10 PC: make sure it's still getting patches
item.description: Microsoft will keep shipping security fixes through October 12, 2027—but only to enrolled PCs. And many desktops that "can't run" Windows 11 just have one setting turned off. — Heads-up: Chrome 157 fixes 213 flaws, seven of them critical

item.title: Don't ignore your browser's certificate warning
item.description: What “Your connection is not private” means, how an attacker could exploit it, and what to check before you continue. — Heads-up: Firefox 159.0.1 fixes a high-impact security flaw

item.title: Your laptop is already encrypted. Do you know where the key is?
item.description: Windows and macOS encrypt your drive with barely a prompt. That protects you if it's stolen, but if it ever asks for the recovery key and you don't have it, your files are gone. — Critical: WordPress: update-process flaw now under attack

item.title: Your TV knows what you're watching
item.description: What automatic content recognition is, why it works even with your console or laptop plugged in over HDMI, and how to turn it off in five minutes. — Critical: Ivanti Connect Secure: corporate VPN hit by chained flaws | Critical: PHP2Shell: two critical PHP flaws added to the exploited list | Heads-up: Android: November patch fixes a critical zero-click flaw
